The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem at a node with:
- Green stem (while surrounding leaves are yellowed/senescing)
- Gray-white fluffy/cottony growth at the node junction
- Yellow/brown fallen leaves in background

Top candidates: **White_Mold** (fluffy mycelial growth at nodes) or **Green_stem_disorder** (green stem with senesced leaves). Let me check reference images.
The White_Mold reference shows fluffy white mycelial growth at nodes - very similar to the test image. Let me check a couple more candidates to be thorough.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem at a node with:
- **Green stem** while surrounding leaves are yellowed (senescent)
- **Fluffy gray-white cottony growth at the node junction** - the most diagnostic feature
- Yellow/fallen leaves in background

**Comparison:**
- **White_Mold**: Reference images show characteristic fluffy white mycelial growth at stem nodes - matches the test image precisely
- **Green_stem_disorder**: Shows green stems with mature pods but no mycelial growth - doesn't match
- **Diaporthe**: Shows dark brown stems with black pycnidia, no fluffy growth - doesn't match
- **Anthracnose**: Dark lesions on pods/stems, no fluffy growth - doesn't match
- **SDS/Phytophthora**: Root/foliar symptoms, no node-level mycelium - doesn't match

The gray-white fluffy/cottony mold at the node on an otherwise green stem is the classic diagnostic sign of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot).
